summary: Elevated 5xx + timeouts for chat completions in us-west; failover trigger did not engage quickly
description:
Customer report (via Support portal):

Company: Mosaic Health (Enterprise)
Time window: 2025-02-07 16:05–17:10 UTC (intermittent continuing at time of ticket)
Region: us-west
Symptoms:
- Elevated HTTP 5xx (mostly 503/504) on /v1/chat/completions
- Increased request latency and client timeouts (reported 20–60s, occasional >60s)
- Some streaming connections dropping mid-response

Customer impact:
- Production user-facing chat feature degraded; customers seeing retries and occasional failures
- Mosaic reports retry storms increased their token spend and caused cascading latency in their app

Customer-provided details:
- Request IDs (sample): rwreq_01HPZ0E7T8W2W2J1QKJ7X9JH0A, rwreq_01HPZ0G2KM2Q9GQ4P7D8K3S9ZN
- SDK: python 0.18.4
- Model: rw-chat-llama-70b (pinned)
- They are region-pinned to us-west for data locality

Initial triage notes:
- Internal dashboards show a us-west error-rate spike and tail-latency increase starting ~16:03 UTC.
- Failover automation appears not to have transitioned to FAILOVER for Mosaic’s traffic; system remained in degraded/monitoring state longer than expected.

Asks from customer:
1) Confirmation of incident scope and status
2) ETA for mitigation
3) Why automatic failover didn’t kick in sooner / what protections exist for enterprise traffic

Internal links used during triage:
- Region health overview: grafana://dashboards/region-health?region=us-west
- Routing/failover state: grafana://dashboards/failover-state?region=us-west
- API errors: datadog://apm/services/api-gateway/errors?region=us-west

Next steps (Support):
- Coordinate with SRE/Platform on mitigation (routing policy adjustments, capacity check)
- Provide customer update + recommended temporary workaround (if needed) while we stabilize
comments: 2025-02-07 17:18 UTC — Dev Patel (Support): Creating incident ticket based on Mosaic escalation. Looping in #incidents with request IDs. Customer is region-pinned to us-west; asks whether we can fail over without violating their locality requirement. Posting link to this ticket in Slack thread: slack://incidents/1709664012

2025-02-07 17:26 UTC — Owen Phillips (Support): Ack. Pulling gateway logs for sample request IDs + checking routing decisions. Initial glance: many 504s from gateway upstream timeout; not an auth/quota issue. Paging SRE on-call for us-west.

2025-02-07 17:34 UTC — Tomáš Novák (SRE): Seeing elevated p99 and 5xx in us-west inference pool starting 16:03 UTC. Cluster health is 'degraded' but not 'failed' per current region evaluator. Queue depth and GPU saturation spiked; looks like partial capacity impairment + some upstream dependency flakiness.

Failover automation status: monitor-only for most routes; no auto transition. Manual failover considered but target us-east capacity headroom was borderline earlier; now improving. Investigating safe-to-failover checks and thresholds.

2025-02-07 17:41 UTC — Miles Thornton (SRE): Confirmed: trigger engine would not have fired on current thresholds because (a) error rate window crossed threshold briefly but did not sustain long enough and (b) hysteresis/hold-down prevented a fast transition during flappy period. This is consistent with known gap from recent incident review: detection is late for short, sharp degradations.

Immediate mitigation option: progressive failover for enterprise tier only (5–10%) to validate capacity + customer experience, then ramp. Need routing/Platform sign-off.

2025-02-07 17:52 UTC — Mina Haddad (Platform / Smart Routing): Approved for progressive reroute for Mosaic traffic as exception. We can apply a scoped policy for customer ID + route. Please keep it reversible. Also noting that Mosaic is pinned to us-west—confirm with Support that cross-region processing is acceptable during incident (temporary) and document in incident notes.

2025-02-07 18:05 UTC — Owen Phillips (Support): Customer confirmed temporary cross-region processing is acceptable during incident mitigation (they prefer availability over locality). Executed scoped routing policy change to allow spillover to us-east for Mosaic; starting at 10% and monitoring. Customer update sent via email + portal: 'degraded performance in us-west; mitigation in progress; next update in 30 minutes.'

2025-02-07 18:22 UTC — Aisha Bello (SRE): Metrics update: For Mosaic requests, 5xx reduced from ~6–9% to <1% after scoped spillover; p95 improving. us-west overall still degraded; not comfortable failing over all traffic. This ticket is a good example of why we need burn-rate aligned triggers; the error budget burn in the first ~20 min was significant even though the longer window smoothed it out.

2025-02-07 19:10 UTC — Tomáš Novák (SRE): us-west stabilized after capacity rebalancing + restarted a hot pod set in one GPU pool; error rate back to baseline. Keeping spillover policy for Mosaic at 10% for another hour, then revert to full us-west if stable. Capturing follow-up items: adjust trigger thresholds/windows; add dedicated/enterprise tier weighting; document when to choose graceful degradation vs failover.

2025-02-08 00:40 UTC — Owen Phillips (Support): Reverted Mosaic routing back to us-west after 2h stable baseline. No further customer-reported errors. Customer asked for RCA-style summary and what’s changing to prevent repeat. Drafting response referencing upcoming failover automation upgrades (without over-committing).

2025-02-08 16:15 UTC — Dev Patel (Support): Sent customer-facing summary: partial regional impairment in us-west caused increased timeouts/5xx; we applied temporary cross-region routing while stabilizing capacity; service returned to normal. Also noted improvements underway: standardized region health signals + safer, faster progressive failover triggers (audited, guardrailed). Ticket marked Resolved.

Follow-ups tracked outside Jira Support:
- Linear: ENG-2844 (trigger evaluation logic), ENG-2845 (safe-to-failover checks)
- Confluence: update automated failover runbook with 'enterprise scoped spillover' guidance
resolution: Mitigated via scoped progressive spillover routing for Mosaic (enterprise) from us-west to us-east (10%) while us-west capacity was stabilized; then reverted when region returned to baseline. Root cause attributed to partial capacity impairment and elevated queue depth in us-west leading to gateway upstream timeouts. Automation did not trigger because thresholds/windows + hysteresis did not classify as 'failed' quickly enough.
